did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with Job’s three friends no longer answering him, because Job remained righteous in his own eyes.
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite is angry with Job because, in his view, Job justified himself rather than God.
Elihu is also angry with Job’s friends because they could not answer him, yet still declared him guilty.
Elihu explains that he remained silent at first because he was younger than the men seated before him, and therefore treated them with respect and caution.
According to Elihu, understanding does not come from age alone; it is the human spirit and the breath of the Almighty that give a person insight.
Elihu describes how he waited patiently, listened to the friends’ words, and examined their arguments until they had finished speaking.
When the friends fall silent and no longer reply, Elihu decides to speak for himself and present his own contribution.
Elihu compares the words and feelings within him to new wine kept in a sealed container, which may burst because of the pressure.
Elihu declares that he will speak without flattering anyone or giving a person undeserved titles of honor.
At the end of the chapter, Elihu says that he does not know how to flatter and warns that flattery could bring punishment upon him from his Maker.
